他把这些指控解释为“一个对公职人员心存疑虑的共同体”的产物，并认为董事会成员缺乏“承受公职人员通常要面对的压力和轻视的韧性”。这一解释恰好反映了董事会成员自己的看法。“人们不知感恩，”其中一人向作者抱怨说。“他们对掌权的人相当多疑。如果董事会成员修理自家屋顶、买一头水牛或改良自己的土地，他们就认为他在利用合作社的公款谋取私利。”作者得出结论说，这些人“过度敏感”。“对他们记录的批评和怀疑只来自少数激进分子。”

en: On the other hand, given the author’s situation, we learn little about these “militant few.” The accusations against the cooperative came from a group led by “a tractor driver in need of a job, having been laid off from the Kura farm.”

But we discover nothing about, say, his treatment as an employee, the reasons he was fired, the poverty he may suffer, or the prospects for such a “militant” of ever finding other employment. The focus of the study is on the village elite (even though they too constitute, of course, only “a few”), and inevitably it is through their eyes that the author sees the village. Still more reflective of the author’s situation in the village is the exclusion from the study of women. “Because I observed no involvement on the part of women in the public affairs of the community,” the author explains, “and because of practical research limitations, women were not included in the survey.”

What is termed a question of practical research limitations is actually the theoretical issue of the author’s status as an outsider and a male. One consequence of this status is the researcher’s conception of politics as “public affairs,” meaning activities that are open to the observation of a visiting stranger. The problem in both these cases lies not in the author’s failure to report the views of the unemployed or to gain access to the women’s realm. Given his situation in the village, this was probably inevitable. It lies in our willingness to accept an account that says almost nothing about the poor and excludes all reference to the experience of women as a picture of “the structures of power in the community.”
Once again one must wonder, given the exclusions, how any evidence of the experience of violence among these groups could find its way into the picture.
zh: 另一方面，鉴于作者的处境，我们对这些“少数激进分子”知之甚少。对合作社的指控来自一个由“一名需要工作的拖拉机手”领导的小组，他“被库拉家的农场解雇了”。
但例如，我们无从得知他作为雇员的待遇、被解雇的原因、他可能遭受的贫困，或者这样一名“激进分子”找到其他工作的前景。研究的焦点是村庄精英（当然，他们同样也只是“少数”），作者不可避免地通过他们的眼睛来看村庄。更能反映作者在村中处境的，是妇女被排除在研究之外。“因为我没有观察到妇女参与共同体的公共事务，”作者解释说，“也因为实际研究的限制，妇女未被纳入调查。”
所谓实际研究限制的问题，实际上是作者作为外来者和男性的地位这一理论问题。这一地位的一个后果，是研究者把政治理解为“公共事务”，即对来访陌生人开放观察的活动。这两种情况的问题都不在于作者未能报告失业者的观点，或未能进入妇女的领域。鉴于他在村中的处境，这或许是不可避免的。问题在于我们愿意接受一种对穷人几乎只字不提、完全排除妇女经验的叙述，作为“共同体权力结构”的图景。
人们不得不再次追问：鉴于这些排除，这些群体中任何关于暴力经验的证据又怎能进入图景？

en: There is a further aspect to the method of positioning the author in relation to his object. To establish the objectness of the village, and thereby the author’s separation from it, the village has to be constructed as something object-like, available to external observation. This means construing it as a system of behaviors, something visible to an observer. Its visibility is contrasted to the invisibility of ideas, which are converted into visible form by assuming them to consist merely of individual attitudes and recording these in a questionnaire. Behavioralism is a more recent form of the positivism that animated the cartographers conducting the cadastral survey at the start of the twentieth century. Its use in political analysis was criticized well before Harik’s study was written (although such criticisms often end up presenting the same material/mental dualism in more sophisticated form).
My purpose here is to relate this issue to the representation of violence. For reasons I will try to explain, such attempts at representation can never capture a culture of fear.
zh: 把作者与研究对象相对定位的方法还有一个方面。要确立村庄的客体性，从而确立作者与村庄的分离，就必须把村庄建构为某种类似客体的东西，可供外部观察。这意味着把它解释为一套行为系统，某种观察者可见的东西。它的可见性与观念的不可见性相对，而观念通过设想其仅由个人态度构成并在问卷中记录，被转化为可见形式。行为主义是20世纪初主持地籍测量的制图师们所信奉的实证主义的一种较新形式。早在哈里克的研究写成之前，它在政治分析中的使用就受到批评（尽管这类批评往往以更精致的形式呈现同样的物质/精神二元论）。
我在这里的目的是把这一问题与暴力的再现联系起来。出于我将试图解释的原因，这类再现尝试永远无法捕捉一种恐惧文化。

en: First, coercion may be articulated in the form of practices that can be reduced neither to observable behavior nor to individual opinions accessible by questionnaire. For example, people in Shubra share a “cultural norm of dignity and self-respect,” we are told, expressed not simply in personal attitudes but in a system of deferential practices, appropriate behaviors, and patterns of modesty.

Such practices can operate as a subtle force of coercion, by which dominant families exercise what Bourdieu calls “symbolic violence”—those forms of obligation and compulsion that are never recognized as coercive but are experienced as generosity, piety, personal loyalty, or self-respect.

The local elections of 1968 in Shubra were governed by such expectations, which impeded active campaigning and helped ensure the victory of the Kuras, thanks to their large accumulation of credit (Bourdieu’s “symbolic capital”) in the system of cultural coercion. This invisible kind of coercion cannot be understood from an observation of the behavior involved, which will appear simply as politeness or decorum. Nor can it be revealed by a survey of attitudes, since the essence of symbolic violence is that it is never recognized as such, but is experienced as a system of morality.
zh: 第一，强制可能以这样一些实践的形式表达出来：它们既不能化约为可观察的行为，也不能化约为可通过问卷获得的个人意见。例如，我们得知，舒卜拉的人共享一种“尊严与自尊的文化规范”，它不仅表现在个人态度中，也表现在一套恭敬的实践、得体的行为和谦逊的模式中。
这类实践可以作为一种微妙的强制力发挥作用，支配家族借此行使布迪厄所说的“象征暴力”——那些从未被认作强制、却被体验为慷慨、虔诚、个人忠诚或自尊的义务与压迫形式。
1968年舒卜拉的地方选举就受这类期待的支配，它们妨碍了积极的竞选活动，并帮助确保了库拉家族的胜利，因为库拉家族在文化强制体系中积累了大量的信用（布迪厄的“象征资本”）。这种无形的强制无法从对相关行为的观察中理解，因为行为只会显得像礼貌或礼节。它也无法通过态度调查揭示，因为象征暴力的本质在于它从不被认作暴力，而是被体验为一套道德体系。

en: Second, attitudes themselves can express far more than they actually say, particularly in the case of those living within the coercive constraints of poverty or political oppression. Although The Political Mobilization of Peasants reports little of the views of poorer villagers, there is much to be read from what they tell us. The book reproduces part of the transcript of an interview with a fifty-five-year-old farmer, ʿAbd al-Mawla. It begins as the author poses question number eight from his survey, concerning the activities in the village of the ASU Leadership Group.
zh: 第二，态度本身所表达的东西可能远远多于其字面所言，对于那些生活在贫困或政治压迫的强制约束中的人尤其如此。尽管《农民的政治动员》很少报告较贫穷村民的看法，但从他们告诉我们的东西中却可以读出许多。该书转载了对五十五岁农民阿卜杜勒-毛拉访谈记录的一部分。访谈从作者提出调查问卷第八个问题开始，内容涉及阿拉伯社会主义联盟领导小组在村中的活动。

en: “I don’t know anything about them.” “You mean you have never heard of them?” “I have, but I do not know anything about them. I just mind my own business.”
zh: “我对他们一无所知。”“你是说你从没听说过他们？”“听说过，但我对他们一无所知。我只管自己的事。”

en: “How did you hear about them?” “From my children.” He paused for a moment and then said, “I am told they go to meetings and talk politics. They want to appear like big people.”
zh: “你是怎么听说他们的？”“听我的孩子们说的。”他停顿了一下，然后说：“有人告诉我，他们去开会，谈论政治。他们想显得像大人物。”

en: “You don’t think this is right for them to do?”
zh: “你不认为他们这样做是对的吗？”

en: “A peasant should not mix with such things. This is the big people’s job. These men have left their fields unattended and are going around doing things that are none of their business.”
zh: “农民不该掺和这种事。这是大人物的事。这些人丢下自家的田地不管，四处去做与他们无关的事。”

en: We changed the subject and talked about village problems. “There are no problems,” he said. “We just need a bakery,” he added. “Not much grain these days in the village, and people baking at home are causing fires.”
zh: 我们换了话题，谈论村里的问题。“没有问题，”他说。“我们只是需要一家面包房，”他补充道。“如今村里粮食不多，在家烤面包的人又常引起火灾。”

en: “You think you can do something about it?” “No, I am a poor man and nobody listens to a poor man.”
zh: “你觉得你能为此做点什么吗？”“不能，我是个穷人，没有人听穷人的话。”

en: Answers of this sort reveal little about “attitudes,” and therefore seem to support conclusions about the absence of political consciousness among the poor. But these statements reveal several things that they do not consciously say. First there is the evident apprehension. ʿAbd al-Mawla “was courteous though ill at ease” during the interview, we are told, and each of his answers begins in the negative and expresses an unwillingness to speak: “I don’t know anything about them”; “There are no problems.” When he does consent to speak, his answers express more than anything else a sense of powerlessness: “I just mind my own business”; “A peasant should not mix with such things”; “Nobody listens to a poor man.” We cannot gauge from this brief transcript the degree of apprehension or fear, the extent of powerlessness or its causes, or the local forms of violence of which these words might be an indirect expression. What we can judge, however, is that a culture of fear will never emerge from the measurement of attitudes.
zh: 这类回答几乎揭示不了什么“态度”，因此似乎支持关于穷人缺乏政治意识的结论。但这些话揭示了若干它们并未有意识说出的东西。首先是明显的忧虑。我们得知，阿卜杜勒-毛拉在访谈中“彬彬有礼，但局促不安”，他的每个回答都以否定开头，表达出不愿说话：“我对他们一无所知”；“没有问题。”当他确实愿意开口时，他的回答表达的首先是一种无力感：“我只管自己的事”；“农民不该掺和这种事”；“没有人听穷人的话。”我们无法从这段简短的记录中衡量忧虑或恐惧的程度、无力感的深浅及其原因，或这些话可能间接表达的当地暴力形式。然而，我们可以判断的是，恐惧文化永远不会从态度的测量中呈现出来。

en: A connection emerges, therefore, between the methods of analysis required by the stance of objectivity and the disappearance of any sign of violence. On the one hand, the writer’s position as an outsider within the village makes his writing tend to portray the experience of the wealthier male landowner at the expense of the experience of women or the poor. On the other hand, the convention of reducing meanings to those ideas available to individual villagers and expressible in the form of attitudes, so that they may be collected from questionnaires or interviews, tends to exclude the possibility of representing the experience of violence. Those who live intolerable lives, coping with poverty, unemployment, hunger, and other, more direct forms of coercion, must somehow express their condition and yet may be unable to find the opportunity, the courage, or the language to do so. These are conditions that may express themselves not in attitudes or accounts of observable events, but in silences, an unwillingness to respond, or the sheer inability to narrate. None of this can be explored by the conventional methods of political analysis found in the works on rural Egypt.
zh: 因此，客观性立场所需的分析方法与暴力迹象的消失之间出现了一种联系。一方面，作者作为村内外来者的位置，使他的写作倾向于描绘较富裕男性地主的经验，而牺牲妇女或穷人的经验。另一方面，把意义化约为个体村民可获得、能以态度形式表达、因而可从问卷或访谈中收集的观念，这一惯例倾向于排除再现暴力经验的可能性。那些过着无法忍受的生活、应对贫困、失业、饥饿和其他更直接强制形式的人，必须以某种方式表达自己的处境，却可能找不到机会、勇气或语言。这些处境可能不是通过态度或对可观察事件的叙述来表达，而是通过沉默、不愿回应或根本无力叙述来表达。这一切都无法用关于埃及乡村的著作中那种常规政治分析方法来探讨。

en: A close reading of some of the American literature on rural politics in Nasserist Egypt has shown how the kind of narrative a particular work adopts can determine whether, and in what way, the question of rural violence is represented. An account of cultural or psychological obstacles to development, a narrative of change, an analysis of interacting individuals, and the construction of an objective view of political behavior and attitudes can in each case transform what evidence there may be of violence into some other pathology, or render its effects invisible. This kind of writing contrasts starkly with the report on the violence of Ahmad Hasan ʿAbdun. The report is an isolated document, the by-product of an attempt to dissipate broader forms of popular discontent, accidentally preserved in the archives. There is no need to suppose that its story is representative of agrarian relations in Egypt in that period, or even reliable evidence for the particular case it records. But the report does have an important use. Its unsettling details challenge us to reexamine the way Western scholars have represented rural political life in Egypt during the crucial struggles of the 1960s, and to question the almost total absence of any sign of, and certainly any investigation of, local violence against the poor.
zh: 对关于纳赛尔时期埃及乡村政治的若干美国文献的细读表明，一部著作所采用的叙述类型可以决定乡村暴力问题是否得到再现以及如何得到再现。关于发展的文化或心理障碍的记述、变迁的叙述、对互动个人的分析，以及对政治行为和态度的客观观点的建构，每一种都能把可能存在的暴力证据转化为别的某种病理，或使其效果不可见。这种写作与关于艾哈迈德·哈桑·阿卜敦暴行的报告形成鲜明对照。这份报告是一份孤立的文件，是试图消解更广泛民众不满的副产品，偶然保存在档案中。无需假定它的故事代表了那个时期埃及的农业关系，甚至无需把它当作其所记录的具体案件的可靠证据。但这份报告确实有一个重要用途。它令人不安的细节促使我们重新审视西方学者在1960年代关键斗争期间再现埃及乡村政治生活的方式，并质疑为何针对穷人的地方暴力几乎完全没有任何迹象，更不用说调查了。

The study of rural rebellion was revived by postcolonial theory in the 1980s and 1990s following the influence of the work of Ranajit Guha, Elementary Aspects of Peasant Insurgency in Colonial India (Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1983) and the Subaltern Studies School. Scott, however, examines the behavior of the poor to find signs of an otherwise unnoticed spirit of peasant resistance, an approach I find problematic (see Mitchell, “Everyday Metaphors of Power”). I am suggesting that one can examine the same practices for signs of otherwise unnoticed forms of domination. For the latter argument, see Lila Abu-Lughod, “The Romance of Resistance,” American Ethnologist 17, no. 1 (1990): 41–55.
zh: 这些论述可能暗示一种类似 Scott, Weapons of the Weak 的方法。然而，斯科特考察穷人的行为，以寻找否则不会被注意到的农民反抗精神迹象，我认为这种方法有问题（见 Mitchell, “Everyday Metaphors of Power”）。我建议的是，可以从同样的实践中寻找否则不会被注意到的支配形式的迹象。后一种论点见 Lila Abu-Lughod, “The Romance of Resistance,” American Ethnologist 17, no. 1 (1990): 41–55.

en: Harik remained, however, one of the most optimistic writers on Egyptian rural development. en: The alleged discovery of evidence that a secret “organization” of the Muslim Brotherhood was plotting to overthrow the regime, evidence the Ministry of the Interior refused to believe, had enabled the military to intervene instead, ordering the widespread arrests and thus extending its own domestic influence as well as its control over the apparatus of government. en: John Waterbury reported an alternative version of the Kamshish story that was later put in circulation, according to which Salah Husain was murdered at the behest of his wife, who hoped to marry into the large landowning family. John Waterbury, The Egypt of Nasser and Sadat: The Political Economy of Two Regimes (Princeton, N.J.: Princeton University Press, 1983), 340.Although Waterbury appeared to lend credence to the story, it was clearly a fabrication, illustrating how political grievances can be delegitimized by transforming them into personal slurs against the victim, the slur depending on the old tactic of impugning the morals of a woman. There is sufficient evidence in the documents collected in Muhammad Rashad, Sirri jiddan, and in the appendix to Ansari, Egypt: The Stalled Society, to corroborate Ansari’s version of the story. I discussed these events with Salah Husain’s widow, Shahinda Maqlad, in May 1993.
zh: 约翰·沃特伯里报告了后来流传的卡姆希什事件的另一种版本，称萨拉赫·侯赛因是在其妻子授意下被谋杀的，后者希望嫁入大地主家族。John Waterbury, The Egypt of Nasser and Sadat: The Political Economy of Two Regimes (Princeton, N.J.: Princeton University Press, 1983), 340. 尽管沃特伯里似乎相信这一说法，它显然是捏造，说明政治怨情如何能通过变成针对受害者的个人诽谤而被去合法化，而诽谤依赖的是诋毁女人道德的旧手段。Muhammad Rashad, Sirri jiddan 所收集的文件以及 Ansari, Egypt: The Stalled Society 的附录中有足够证据佐证安萨里的版本。1993年5月，我与萨拉赫·侯赛因的遗孀沙欣达·马克拉德讨论过这些事件。

en: According to Harik’s figures, only 44 percent of the village’s adult males cultivate their own land, leaving 56 percent who make their living by other means. It is not clear what proportion of the latter have adequate incomes from other sources and what proportion form the “landless” poor to whom I am referring. Harik, Political Mobilization, 290, table 2. My figure of 40 percent is obtained from the table by adding together 100 percent of “agricultural laborers” with 70 percent of “craftsmen and tradesmen” and 70 percent of “native employees” (70 percent being my estimate of the proportion of these two groups earning less than the poverty level of E£12 per month [see note 57, below], based on the income figures given on p. 47), totaling 539, or 40 percent of the adult male population of 1,350. This figure may underestimate the proportion of families living in poverty, for two reasons: the survey excludes women, even those heading a household—Radwan and Lee’s survey of 18 villages found that 8.5 percent of rural households were female-headed and that such households ranked among the poorest (Agrarian Change in Egypt, 64, table 4.10)—and it excludes those who own or rent land, but in amounts too small to keep them out of poverty.
